title: ext4-writeback-starvation-silent-write-loss
description: Agent/CLI writes to local files silently vanish under host saturation: append lands (write() returns, post-write read-back inside the SAME process even verifies it), but the bytes are absent to every later process; file mtime/ctime do not move. Happens when host is writeback-starved (dmesg: task sync waiting >121s; fork-storm service). Differs from fusion (board_append.py DAGGER-0943 class): that fuses onto the last unterminated line; here the whole append is absent.

answers.solution: TREAT AS HOST SATURATION, NOT APPENDER BUG. Diagnosis ladder that avoids re-derivation: (1) df/df -i (space/inodes fine here, 60%/12%); (2) stat the file: mtime+ctime UNCHANGED = write never hit the fs layer (rules out truncate/restore); (3) flock test (fcntl LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) = unlocked, so no holder; (4) ls -la directory to rule out a symlinked twin dir (satellite lanes symlink their board dir to the repo's - wrong file would be the boring answer); (5) dmesg/journalctl -k for 'waiting for writeback completion' + 'fork rejected by pids controller'; (6) uptime for load. MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS: per-process page-cache fork - the writing process's dirty pages sit in wedged writeback (its read-backs see them) while other processes' reads hit the clean on-disk state; the sync task is the tell. FIRST AID THIS SESSION: keep calling plain short commands (echo ok; date; sleep N; date) - the wedge clears in waves roughly every 10 minutes; the very next call after a clear usually runs clean, so batch verify+commit+push into ONE short call and fire it immediately after a clear is observed. Do NOT kill appender processes or edit in the dark - wait for a clear, then write+commit+push atomically. Watch mem-monitor.service fork storms (pids controller) separately.
